claims.text: Multiphase refractory high-entropy alloys with particular positive mixing enthalpies will exhibit a ductile-brittle-ductile transition during aging.
The non-monotonic ductility transition is driven by sequential short-range ordering, phase precipitation, and subsequent dissolution or coarsening of ordered phases.
Al0.5NbTa0.8Ti1.5V0.2Zr is an example of the proposed BCC-based multiphase RHEA family.
The initial alloy contains disordered BCC and ordered B2 or Heusler-type phases.
The initial alloy contains short-range-order clusters.
Isothermal aging at 600–800 °C over varying durations can induce phase evolution and chemical ordering in the proposed alloys.
The aging temperature must activate ordering diffusion while remaining below the secondary-phase solvus.
An inert atmosphere is necessary to prevent oxidation from interfering with the aging response.
Chemical ordering evolves from SRO clusters to long-range-ordered precipitates and then to coarsened or dissolved ordered phases.
Initial SRO clusters moderately impede dislocations while retaining cross-slip and ductility.
Positive elemental mixing enthalpies can provide a thermodynamic driving force for precipitation.
Aging produces coherent long-range-ordered precipitates that obstruct glide, promote planar slip, and cause brittle fracture.
Prolonged aging causes ordered precipitates to coarsen or partially dissolve, lowering the density of coherent obstacles.
The reduced obstacle density permits Orowan looping or cross-slip and thereby restores ductility.
Elongation to failure versus aging time will form a U-shaped curve whose minimum coincides with peak ordering or precipitate density.
AlxCrCoFeNi exhibits extensive chemical clustering over a broad temperature range when x is below 0.5.
The x < 0.5 result in AlxCrCoFeNi defines a composition boundary for a ductile-brittle-ductile transition in multiphase RHEAs.
Alloys having purely negative mixing enthalpies are outside the transition regime because they immediately form stable intermetallics.
Phase instability observed at 700 °C after 1000 hours could prevent long-time ductility recovery, although the cited observation is from Cr18Mn27Fe27.5Ni27.5 rather than the proposed RHEA.
The mechanical role of Heusler-type phases remains unclear.
